course.title: Interior Decoration Basics
course.tagline: Style rooms beautifully: colour, layout and finishing touches on any budget.

days.title: Interior Decoration Basics
days.goal: Know what interior decoration is: colour, layout, light and texture.

video.title: 13 Design Tricks to Instantly Make Small Spaces Look BIGGER

steps: Learn that decoration is how a room looks and feels, not how it is built.
Learn the four parts: colour, layout, light and texture.
Learn that texture is how a surface feels: smooth, rough, soft.
Look at a room and name its colour, layout, light and texture.
days.task: Name the four parts of decoration in a room you know.
days.challenge: Explain texture in plain words.

quiz.q: What are the four parts of interior decoration?
quiz.explain: Decoration is colour, layout, light and texture working together.

quiz.q: What is texture in a room?
options: How a surface feels: smooth, rough or soft
quiz.explain: Texture is the feel of surfaces, like a soft rug or a rough brick wall.

quiz.q: What does decoration change?
options: How a room looks and feels
quiz.explain: Decoration changes how a room looks and feels, not its structure.

days.title: Colour: Warm and Cool
days.goal: Tell warm and cool colours apart and know what each does.

video.title: 13 Design Tricks to Instantly Make Small Spaces Look BIGGER

steps: Warm colours are red, orange and yellow: they feel cosy.
Cool colours are blue, green and purple: they feel calm.
Light colours make a room feel bigger.
Dark colours make a room feel smaller and cosier.
days.task: Sort colours into warm and cool.
days.challenge: Pick a colour for a small bedroom and explain why.

quiz.q: Which colours feel cosy?
quiz.explain: Warm colours like red, orange and yellow feel cosy and welcoming.

quiz.q: Which colours feel calm?
quiz.explain: Cool colours like blue and green feel calm and relaxing.

quiz.q: What do light colours do to a room?
quiz.explain: Light colours reflect light and make a room feel bigger.

days.title: The 60-30-10 Colour Rule
days.goal: Use the 60-30-10 rule to mix colours in a room.

video.title: 13 Design Tricks to Instantly Make Small Spaces Look BIGGER

steps: 60 percent is the main colour: walls and big furniture.
30 percent is the second colour: curtains and chairs.
10 percent is the accent colour: cushions and art.
Pick three colours for a room using the rule.
days.task: Plan a room with the 60-30-10 rule.
days.challenge: Name the three parts of the rule without looking.

quiz.q: What is the 60-30-10 colour rule?
options: 60% main colour, 30% second colour, 10% accent colour
quiz.explain: The rule splits a room into 60% main, 30% second and 10% accent colour.

quiz.q: What is the accent colour for?
options: Small pops of colour like cushions and art
quiz.explain: The accent colour is the small 10% that adds personality.

quiz.q: What is the main colour in a room?
quiz.explain: The main colour covers 60%: walls and big furniture.

quiz.explain: A big mirror bounces light around and makes the room feel bigger.

quiz.q: Why keep furniture low in a small room?
